INTRODUCTION
Zyro Dynamics believes that regular, structured, and honest performance conversations are essential to the
growth of both the individual and the organisation. Our performance management framework is designed to help
employees understand expectations clearly, receive meaningful feedback throughout the year, and be recognised
and rewarded fairly for their contributions. This policy describes the review cycles, rating scales, goal-setting
framework, and the process for managing performance that does not meet expectations.
SCOPE AND APPLICABILITY
This policy applies to all permanent and fixed-term contract employees at Zyro Dynamics. Probationary
employees are subject to the Probation Review process described below. Interns and consultants are not
covered under this policy but may receive informal feedback as part of their engagement.

GOAL SETTING — OKR FRAMEWORK
Zyro Dynamics uses the OKR (Objectives and Key Results) framework for goal setting at all levels of the
organisation. Goals are set at the beginning of each financial year in April and must be documented in the
ZyroHR portal by April 30.
  Objectives are 3 to 5 aspirational goals aligned to the team and company-level OKRs for the year.
 Key Results are 3 to 5 measurable outcomes per objective that define what success looks like in concrete
terms.
 Goals are mutually agreed between the employee and their reporting manager and cannot be set unilaterally
by either party.
 Goals may be revised during the Mid-Year Review if there has been a significant shift in business priorities,
with appropriate documentation.

PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENT PLAN (PIP)
An employee who receives a rating of 1 or 2 in two consecutive review cycles will be placed on a formal
Performance Improvement Plan. The PIP is a structured and time-bound programme aimed at giving the
employee a fair opportunity to improve.
PIP Structure
  Duration: 60 to 90 days, as determined by the reporting manager and HR Business Partner.
 At the start of the PIP, specific, measurable, and time-bound improvement targets are agreed and
documented.
 Weekly check-in meetings between the employee and the manager are mandatory throughout the PIP
period.
 The HR Business Partner will be present at all formal PIP review meetings and will maintain complete
documentation of proceedings.
PIP Outcomes
  Successful completion: The employee exits the PIP and returns to the standard performance management
cycle.
 Partial improvement: The PIP may be extended by up to 30 additional days at the joint discretion of HR and
the manager.
 No improvement: The outcome may include a role change, demotion, or separation in accordance with the
company's disciplinary and separation policy.
PROMOTIONS
Promotions at Zyro Dynamics are merit-based and are reviewed annually as part of the APR cycle. To be
eligible for consideration, an employee must have completed a minimum of 12 months in their current grade,
received a rating of 4 or 5 in the current Annual Performance Review, and demonstrated the competencies
expected at the next grade level as assessed by the manager and calibration committee. For grades L6 and
